title: Superstar-Turned-CM Vijay Just Met Modi for the First Time Since Taking Office. He Brought a List.
excerpt: Tamil Nadu's new Chief Minister raised the Mekedatu dam dispute, jailed fishermen, and the state anthem controversy in a 10-minute meeting that Delhi is still decoding.
body:
C. Joseph Vijay, the Tamil superstar who became Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu less than three weeks ago, made his first official visit to Delhi on Wednesday and sat across from Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a meeting that lasted roughly 10 minutes — but packed enough political signalling to keep analysts in both capitals busy for days.

Vijay arrived at Tamil Nadu House earlier in the day, where he received a ceremonial guard of honour. By evening, Tamil social media was already circulating side-by-side photographs of Wednesday's meeting and an earlier interaction between Vijay and Modi from 2014, long before the actor had formally entered politics. In Tamil Nadu, where visual symbolism often carries more weight than policy documents, the images spoke volumes.

## The List

Vijay did not come to Delhi for small talk. According to the Tamil Nadu government, the Chief Minister raised four politically charged issues, each tied to the state's deep anxieties about federal overreach and regional identity.

**The Mekedatu Dam.** Karnataka's proposed reservoir across the Cauvery river is an existential issue in Tamil Nadu agriculture. Vijay objected to Karnataka's plans for a bhoomi pooja for the project, arguing that it violated both the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal award and Supreme Court rulings. He urged the Centre not to permit the project without the consent of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry, warning that the announcement had triggered "serious concern" among farmers.

**Jailed Fishermen.** Vijay told Modi that 58 Tamil Nadu fishermen are currently in Sri Lankan prisons and hundreds of fishing boats remain seized. He urged the Centre to intensify diplomatic efforts to secure their release — a demand that every Tamil Nadu chief minister has made to every prime minister for decades, and which continues to go largely unresolved.

**The Tamil Anthem.** In the most symbolically loaded item on the list, Vijay raised the recent controversy over the singing of Tamil Thai Vazhthu at central government-linked functions in Tamil Nadu. He sought clarity that the state anthem could continue to be sung before Vande Mataram at official events — an issue that quickly escalated into another chapter in Tamil Nadu's long-running politics of language, identity, and federal assertion.

**Defence and Aviation Infrastructure.** Vijay also pushed for an air navigation centre and defence-linked aviation infrastructure in Tamil Nadu, signalling that his government intends to be more than a single-issue operation.

## The Political Arithmetic

Vijay's political journey from silver screen to Secretariat remains one of the most unusual in Indian politics. His party won 108 seats in the Assembly elections — making it the single largest force — and later secured a confidence vote with support from Congress, CPI, CPI(M), VCK, and IUML legislators. The trust vote itself was dramatic: 25 AIADMK MLAs defected from their party to back the new government.

The coalition is stitched together from parties that contested against Vijay but later rallied behind him to prevent political instability. His Delhi itinerary reflects this arithmetic. Beyond the Modi meeting, Vijay is scheduled to meet Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan, and senior Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, and Mallikarjun Kharge.

## Why the Diaspora Should Watch

For the Tamil diaspora — among the largest and most politically engaged of India's overseas communities — Vijay's ascent represents something genuinely new. He is the first chief minister of Tamil Nadu who is, by any measure, a global cultural figure. His films have been box-office forces across Southeast Asia, and his fan clubs function as parallel civic organizations in cities from Singapore to Toronto.

Whether Vijay can translate star power into governance outcomes is the question that his Delhi visit is meant to begin answering. The Mekedatu dam and the fishermen issue are not new. But having a chief minister who commands the attention of 200 million Tamil speakers — and who can sit across from Modi knowing that the photographs will be parsed in Kuala Lumpur and Colombo as much as in Chennai — is a political variable that Delhi has not had to account for before.

The meeting lasted 10 minutes. The aftershocks will last considerably longer.
